candidates.why: Must Read: compute-matched RL across 4 benchmarks with paired per-task stats, an edits-discarded control isolating the playbook's own contribution, and a chain-vs-group credit ablation — the strongest experimental closure in its area (ACE-RL).
candidates.caveat: Single training run per method and evidence limited to 0.6B/4B models; the MBPP environment leaks its scored assertions, favoring any handoff mechanism.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: cost accounting (3-4x RSI tax, verification at 74.8-93.6%) is solid and important, but the headline 'SRN matches accuracy' rests on single-run point estimates with no seeds, and compared systems are weakened streaming adaptations.
candidates.caveat: No repeated runs or variance estimates; several headline accuracy gaps (1-3 points) could be noise, so 'matches or exceeds' should be read as point-estimate comparisons.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: clean paired-seed demonstration with exact tests, but scope is one synthetic 3-variable system, two agents, and a no-tools harness; the area's top candidate (ACE-RL) has far stronger experimental evidence.
candidates.caveat: Prompt-harness confound: real AI-scientist deployments let agents compute uncertainty maps or run space-filling designs; the demonstrated failure is a property of this harness.

candidates.why: Must Read: production-scale evidence — 61 problems (32 silent) across 13 framework-model combinations with noise-calibrated thresholds (clean <=3.44x floor vs defective >=4.35x) and 42 confirmed upstream fixes (Plumbline).
candidates.caveat: No false-negative analysis; calibration is done on known defects only, so Plumbline finds many silent faults but does not certify correctness.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: exceptionally rigorous causal chain (5-seed replication, norm replays, trajectory swaps), but headline 1.4B/3.4B margins are single-seed and thin relative to the measured +/-0.0028-nat seed noise, and a linear-taper baseline beats the celebrated window.
candidates.caveat: Many headline comparisons — including the entire 1.4B and 3.4B tables — use a single seed; 0.002-0.01-nat margins are within plausible noise of the seed spread.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: solid method paper (tuned baselines, 3 seeds, per-component ablations, released code) but evidence caps at 1.3B/22B tokens with downstream scores near noise — below the bar set by its area's production-scale evidence.
candidates.caveat: Experiments cap at 1.3B parameters and 22B training tokens; PIQA scores at this scale are close to chance and downstream differences are hard to distinguish from noise.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: flawless statistical hygiene (exact enumeration, 10 seeds per cell, per-prompt-copy controls, released code), but the setting is a 101k-parameter toy on 64 prompts where a 'shared error' is an identical string — no real-LLM validation of the mechanism.
candidates.caveat: Tiny synthetic setting: two-token responses, 64 prompts, one architecture; the reconciliation of prior conflicting studies remains an untested hypothesis.

candidates.why: Must Read: a falsifiable, pre-measurable threshold (pr/b > 1) that held in all seven conditions across three real task families on 1.5-3.8B models, backed by a lottery causal control and a pre-registered depth-3 prediction that was borne out (Honesty Is a Race).
candidates.caveat: Single seeds at most bracket ends and every MBPP code run is single-seed; the code threshold is only loosely bracketed because intermediate runs were still recovering when training stopped.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: certified-conflict environments and bidirectional transfer tests are well-designed, but all evidence rests on one 4B model and one RL algorithm, the lambda=1 penalty is not ablated, and external-benchmark results are illustrative subsets.
candidates.caveat: Single 4B model (Qwen3.5-4B) and a single RL algorithm (GRPO); scale dependence of the misalignment delta is explicitly untested.

candidates.why: Must Read: paired six-model study with exact McNemar/Wilcoxon tests, pre-registered criteria with failures reported, and a same-width stochastic-rounding control that causally separates rounding bias from resolution — plus a zero-overhead fix validated end-to-end (Lost in Rounding).
candidates.caveat: Single seed for most arms; the Nemotron-3 residual bulk shift and the Falcon-H1R-7B null are both unexplained.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: elegant triangulation (DIMM + device + TCAD on ~700k devices) unifying three disturbance modes, but the tail-vs-bulk trap story is a working hypothesis without direct trap observation and TCAD conditions diverge ~9x from the DIMM protocol.
candidates.caveat: The TCAD baseline is calibrated only against array-averaged leakage; this does not by itself establish the distribution of first-failure thresholds.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: exemplary 180-chip real-hardware characterization proving the fastHammer proxy sound (>95% cell overlap), but the headline reliability and 0.9-54.4% speedup numbers come from Monte Carlo/Ramulator models (benign access pattern, DDR5 simulated from DDR4), not measurement.
candidates.caveat: The error model uses a benign uniform-random access pattern; adversarial workloads with knowledge of weak rows could invalidate the P(UE) numbers.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: the deterministic harness-fault scan (45% of hand-crafted Who&When runs end in content-filter crashes) is benchmark-hygiene gold, but the core measurements rest on single-LLM annotation with no human inter-annotator agreement, and the headline control-reach numbers are counterfactual judgments never validated by re-running agents.
candidates.caveat: The counterfactual control-reach judgments were never validated by re-running agents with the controls installed — 'reaches' is analytical, not empirical.

candidates.why: Must Read: oracle validated on held-out fault injection (76% detection, 2% false alarms), mutants, public bugs and dual-rater human review; byte-for-byte replay of all 4,998 executions; and 7 upstream fixes independently re-verified (isloss).
candidates.caveat: The headline 18.5% silent-loss rate is measured on a synthetic suite; on recorded real agent traffic the primary rate drops to 4.1%.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: clean paired-scenario design with a deterministic oracle, but the benchmark is LLM-generated with no artifact release, the three baselines are evaluated in configurations that structurally cannot succeed, and post-repair violation rates stay high where agents ignore the repair prompt.
candidates.caveat: Effectiveness is capped by the agent's response to the repair prompt: on Qwen the ABV rate remains 77.3% after repair, so the worst offenders are least protected.

candidates.why: Must Read: pre-registered measurement study with failed predictions reported, full artifact release, and community cross-checks; cleanly separates 4-bit effects (3.5-5.8% flips) above every non-quantization noise source while 8-bit is inseparable from the floor in 3 of 32 comparisons.
candidates.caveat: Two same-family models on one device (GB10) and only one restart pair per build — the floor, the denominator of every ratio, is the least-certain measured quantity.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: exceptional pre-registration hygiene auditing the second-order quantization screen, but the flagship alignment-flag finding rests on a single cell (Qwen3-32B int4), the MoE test is officially inconclusive, and the throughput criterion was non-discriminating.
candidates.caveat: The tensor-alignment flag and block form are validated by a single cell; no tensor was flagged on the unseen Mistral test, so the flag's real-world firing rate is unknown.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: exemplary pre-registered mechanism work (positive controls isolate persistence; dose-response), but headline gains are conditioned on affected cells by construction, the fix fails on half of DMC and is outright harmful on walker at 3 bits, and the integer path loses to pre-converted BF16.
candidates.caveat: The primary bit width per task is pre-defined as the largest k where det loses >=20 points, so 'median 95% removed' should not be read as an expectation over arbitrary quantization configs.

candidates.why: Must Read: NeurIPS-accepted analysis across 10 LMs, 5 released dictionary families, ViTs and crosscoders; a formal rank-one tiling argument confirmed by interventions, and a verified FVU dominance-factor identity that changes how released SAE fidelity numbers must be read — with a zero-cost post-hoc fix.
candidates.caveat: The importance-side confound is partly an artifact of zero-ablation (support-preserving resample yields 83% sharing pre-bypass on GPT-2); the splice-cost headline is a single-seed best case.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: exact closed-form reduction validated at 96.1% first-token agreement with out-of-sample diagnostics is impressive, but it holds only at the last residual stream — mid-depth steering, where practice operates, is untested — and thresholds rest on one or two crossing models.
candidates.caveat: The closed form holds only for rank-1 ablation at the last residual stream under greedy decoding; whether centring helps at mid-depth layers is untested and explicitly disclaimed.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: good controls and dose-response for a no-hacking-examples steering vector, but evidence rests on 3 mid-size models with 1-2 tasks each, the TACO honeypot has only 5 hacking runs, GPT-OSS fails to separate hacking from honest failure, and effective doses are ~10x the natural rise.
candidates.caveat: Only three mid-size open-weight models with one or two trajectory tasks each; the Qwen TACO honeypot set has just 5 hacking runs.

candidates.why: Must Read: production-stack systems report from the codebase's owners — measured throughput matrix on 16-512 B300 GPUs (1.2T total params at 858 TFLOP/s/GPU), Token Gerrymandering backed by an analytic argument plus a checkpoint-branched experiment, and quantified negative results throughout.
candidates.caveat: Headline Table 30 numbers use random routing (optimistic by up to ~9% with a learned router at EP8); rows co-vary batch/PP/precision, so no single-factor conclusion can be drawn, and no time-to-quality results are reported.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: carefully measured (bitwise-verified, L2-flushed) one-sided EP all-to-all already shipped in FlashInfer3/vLLM/SGLang, but the evaluation is layer-level microbenchmarks under perfect routing with no end-to-end serving numbers, it loses to fused MegaMoE at >=256 tokens/rank, and single-NVLink-domain scope favors its home turf vs DeepEP.
candidates.caveat: Layer-level microbenchmarks with synthetic (perfect or Zipf) routing; no end-to-end serving results, and the FP8-combine accuracy claim is one sentence with no numbers.

candidates.why: Not a Must Read: the largest unified comparison of MoE overlap strategies (103 shapes x 4 platforms) with a cheap closed-form selector, but the average end-to-end gain over the strongest baseline is only 1.78%, headline wins concentrate on mismatched baselines, routing is synthetic (fixed rho=2.0), and nothing is released.
candidates.caveat: Kernel benchmarks use synthetic routing with a fixed imbalance factor of 2.0; real router distributions and intra-rank expert skew are not tested.
